newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economic recovery intact, but needs easy credit.
newsitem.headline: Japan economic recovery intact, but needs easy credit.

text.p: Japan's gradual economic recovery remains intact despite some weakness emerging among businesses, but it still needs the help of easy credit for full recovery, the government said on Friday.

"The economy is continuing to recover, as seen in the increasingly bullish tone in private-sector demand, but the tempo of the recovery is gradual for now," the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) report said.

In a regular report on the health of the economy, the government's economic policy research arm said the recovery was making only slow progress and that it still needed the help of easy credit to reach a self-sustaining stage.
It also prescribed remedies such as deregulation and expansion of domestic demand to nurse the economy back to full health, but stopped short of mentioning any additional fiscal stimulus measures.

Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has said he will decide after the release of April-June gross domestic product data whether or not to draft an extra budget featuring large public works projects around September 20.

However, media reports have said the government may shelve the option in the face of tight state finances, as Japan's average economic growth is expected to show a slight increase in the first half of calendar 1996.
"Economic fundamentals are generally improving, but business sentiment is still cautious, so our overall assessment remains unchanged," an Economic Planning Agency (EPA) official told reporters.

The latest monthly economic report was virtually unchanged in its core evaluation, using the same wording as before. The wording of the report is scrutinised by markets for any hint of growing confidence about the status of the recovery.

The government declared in February that the nation's economy had finally come out of years of slump that followed the collapse of the 1980s "bubble" economy, but the EPA has not been able to strengthen its "gradual recovery" assessment.
"We have not been able to confirm that the current recovery has become a self-sustaining one," the official said.

Although overall business sentiment continues to brighten, some companies have become cautious as can be seen in sluggish growth of industrial output, a high level of inventories and a still worrisome unemployment rate, the EPA official said.
The BOJ's "tankan", released on August 28, also showed the diffusion index for major manufacturers fell to minus seven in August from minus three in the previous survey in May.
But growth in exports has risen as the weakness of the yen against the dollar this past year has helped Japan-made products, especially cars, regain their competitiveness, the EPA official said.
He also noted that the jobless rate, though still at a high level, had come down to 3.4 percent in July after posting a record 3.5 percent for the previous three months.
Asked whether the government had strengthened its economic assessment at all, the EPA official said: "I'd say it has moved just a bit forward."
An increase in corporate capital spending was confirmed by the BOJ's tankan survey and private consumption is recovering as well, helped by a better labour environment, he said.
"Tempo is gradual, but we are heading towards self-sustainable recovery," he said.

But worrisome factors remain, such as a fall off of public works spending later this year and the effect of the planned increase in the consumption tax on the level of house-building and purchase, currently high as people act before the tax increase comes into effect in April.
A sluggish semicondutor market may also force companies to revise down their capital spending plans later this year, the EPA official said.
